title: Reminded by the verses, they fall into prostration.
subtitle: The verse that gives the surah its name
then: The surah is named As-Sajdah after this verse. Ibn Kathir says true believers {idea}listen to the verses and obey them in word and deed{/idea}. They are {reward}not too proud to submit{/reward}, unlike the rebellious who scorn worship.
now: A verse in Taraweeh hits you hard. You feel it in your chest. Then the car park, the traffic, and it is gone. {reward}The believer's response goes all the way down to the floor.{/reward} Sajdah is where a reminder becomes real.
old: Feeling moved by a verse is enough.
new: A reminder is meant to bring me down in sajdah, not just stir me.
try: After your next prayer, stay in one extra sajdah and say subhana rabbiyal a'la slowly.

title: They leave their beds to call their Lord in fear and hope.
subtitle: Night prayer and giving
then: Mujahid and Al-Hasan said this means {idea}voluntary night prayer{/idea}. Ad-Dahhak said Isha and Fajr in congregation. When Mu'adh asked about the gates of goodness, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned {reward}prayer in the depth of the night{/reward} and recited this verse.
now: The alarm for Fajr. The duvet is heavy and warm, and your thumb goes to snooze. {idea}This verse is about that exact moment.{/idea} Getting up is where fear and hope meet.
old: Night prayer is for very pious people, not me.
new: Leaving a warm bed for Allah, even briefly, is the act this verse praises.
try: Tonight, set your alarm ten minutes before Fajr and pray two short rak'ahs.

title: No soul knows the joy kept hidden for them.
subtitle: A hidden reward for hidden deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}because they concealed their good deeds, Allah concealed the reward{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ reported that Allah said He has prepared for His righteous servants {reward}what no eye has seen and no ear has heard{/reward}.
now: You prayed at 4am and told no one. You sent money to a struggling friend with no name on the transfer. {reward}That secret has a secret waiting for it.{/reward} Some things are better kept between you and Allah.
old: If no one knows my good deeds, they barely count.
new: The deeds I hide are the ones Allah answers with a hidden gift.
try: Do one good deed today and tell absolutely no one about it.

title: The believer and the rebel are not equal.
subtitle: Allah's justice does not blur them together
then: Ibn Kathir says that in {idea}His justice and generosity{/idea}, Allah will not judge believers like those who rebelled. Some early scholars said it came about Ali bin Abi Talib and Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt.
now: Your honest colleague gets passed over and the one who cuts corners gets promoted. {trap}It feels like it makes no difference.{/trap} {idea}Allah does not score them the same{/idea}, even when the office does.
old: In the end, good and bad people all get the same.
new: Allah's justice keeps them apart, even when the world mixes them up.
try: Keep doing one honest thing at work today, even if it costs you a little.

title: Gardens of Refuge, a welcome for honoured guests.
subtitle: The believers' home
then: Ibn Kathir says the Gardens hold {reward}dwellings, houses and lofty rooms{/reward}. The word used means {reward}something prepared to welcome and honour a guest{/reward}, given for what they used to do.
now: Think of arriving at your grandmother's house after a long trip. The food is ready, the room is made up, she has been waiting. {reward}That is the word used here.{/reward} The believer arrives as an expected guest.
old: If I make it to Paradise, I will just scrape through.
new: Allah welcomes the believer as an honoured guest He has been waiting for.
try: Welcome a guest or visitor today with real care, and think of this verse.

title: No escape from the Fire they used to deny.
subtitle: The end of those who rebelled
then: Ibn Kathir says those who disobeyed Allah will have the Fire as their dwelling, and {trap}every time they try to escape they are returned{/trap}. They are told to taste {trap}what they used to deny{/trap}.
now: You hear a verse like this and want to skip ahead. Stay with it for a moment. {idea}It is meant for you to still have a choice.{/idea} The door of repentance is open today.
old: Verses about the Fire are only for other people.
new: This warning is a mercy that reaches me while I can still turn back.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one specific thing, and ask Allah to protect you from the Fire.

title: Smaller hardships now, so that they may return.
subtitle: Trials in this world as a wake-up call
then: Ibn Abbas said the nearer punishment means {idea}diseases and problems in this world{/idea}, a test from Allah {idea}so that His servants repent to Him{/idea}. Many early scholars said the same.
now: The car breaks down the week rent is due. A health scare you did not see coming. {idea}It could be a nudge home.{/idea} Before asking why me, ask: is there something I need to turn back from?
old: Bad things in my life are just random.
new: Some hardships are invitations to come back to Allah before it is late.
try: Think of one recent difficulty and ask what it might be calling you back to.

title: Who does more wrong than one reminded who turns away?
subtitle: Turning from a clear reminder

row.title: most misguided, most in need
sub: the one who turns from dhikr

then: Ibn Kathir says no one does more wrong than one who is shown the signs clearly and then {trap}neglects them, as if he does not know them{/trap}. Qatadah said: {idea}beware of turning away from the remembrance of Allah{/idea}.
now: You read the verse about lying, nodded, and lied on the timesheet the same week. {trap}Knowing makes it heavier, not lighter.{/trap} The answer is not to stop reading, but to let the reminder land.
old: If I do not think about the reminder, it does not apply to me.
new: Once I have been reminded, turning away is its own wrong.
try: Pick one reminder you heard this week and act on it today.
